title: Farata with Rairiha (Fish Curry)
description: A traditional Minicoy breakfast of rectangular maida parathas, pan-cooked until golden-brown, served with Rairiha - a fiery red fish curry made with coconut milk, garlic, onions, and chilli powder .
steps: Knead flour with water and a little ghee into a soft dough.
Roll into rectangular parathas and cook on a hot pan until golden-brown on both sides.
Prepare Rairiha: Cook fish with coconut milk, onion, garlic, curry leaves, and chilli powder into a spicy curry.
Serve hot faratas with the fish curry.
tip: Rairiha does not use kokum or tamarind - coconut milk provides the body .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Rairiha does not use kokum or tamarind - coconut milk provides the body .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A popular breakfast combo in Minicoy Island.

title: Kilanji
description: An ultra-thin rice and egg-based crepe paired with a sweet coconut, banana, and jaggery/sugar concoction. A staple at festivities and special gatherings across Lakshadweep .
steps: Soak rice for a few hours, then blend with eggs into a smooth batter .
Strain the batter to ensure a smooth consistency.
Heat a greased pan and pour a thin layer of batter, swirling to cover the pan .
Cook until edges lift, then fold like a crepe or dosa.
Prepare the sauce by mixing coconut milk, sugar/jaggery, and chopped banana .
Top the crepes with the sweet sauce and serve.
tip: Described as 'island simplicity at its finest' - light, creamy, and comforting .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Described as 'island simplicity at its finest' - light, creamy, and comforting .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often served during weddings and festive gatherings .

title: Kiraliappam with Rairiha
description: A popular Minicoy breakfast item - rice-flour pancakes dipped in coconut milk, served with Rairiha (spicy fish curry) .
steps: Make a smooth batter with rice flour and water.
Cook thin pancakes on a hot tawa.
Prepare Rairiha fish curry with coconut milk, onion, garlic, and spices.
Serve the pancakes with the curry for dipping.
tip: The rice-flour pancakes are often dipped in coconut milk before eating .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The rice-flour pancakes are often dipped in coconut milk before eating .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A traditional breakfast in Minicoy Island.

title: Mus Kavaab (Tuna Curry)
description: A signature Minicoy dish - boneless tuna marinated in coconut, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, cardamom, and cloves, then cooked with onions, tomatoes, and curry leaves .
steps: Grind coconut with spice powders, cardamom, and cloves into a fine paste .
Sauté onions and tomatoes with curry leaves until soft.
Add the masala paste and water, bring to a boil.
Add fish chunks and simmer for about 10 minutes until cooked .
Serve hot with steamed rice.

fullIngredients.name: Turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder

tip: 'Mus' means fish and 'kavab' translates to curry .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: 'Mus' means fish and 'kavab' translates to curry .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best paired with steamed rice for a classic meal .

title: Maasu Podichath (Dried Tuna Mix)
description: A traditional Lakshadweep dish where dried tuna (maasu) is ground into fine pieces and mixed with grated coconut, onion, garlic, turmeric, and chilli powder. Served as a side dish with rice or chapathi .
steps: Cut the dried tuna into small pieces.
Grind the pieces until fine .
Transfer to a bowl and add all other ingredients .
Mix well by hand.
Serve with chapathi, pooris, or plain rice .
tip: A versatile dish that goes well with chapathi, pooris, or plain rice .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A versatile dish that goes well with chapathi, pooris, or plain rice .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Dried tuna is a specialty of the Lakshadweep islands .

title: Mas Huni
description: A Maldivian-inspired dish popular in Minicoy - finely chopped tuna mixed with grated coconut, onions, and green chilli. Typically eaten with Malabar Parotta or steamed rice .
steps: Cook tuna and flake it finely.
Mix with grated coconut, onion, green chilli, and salt.
Add a squeeze of lime juice.
Serve with Malabar Parotta or steamed rice.
tip: Popular in Minicoy due to its proximity to Maldives .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Popular in Minicoy due to its proximity to Maldives .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A light, fresh-tasting dish perfect for lunch.

title: Sannath (Slow-Cooked Tuna Curry)
description: A thick semi-fish gravy made with a masala of ground vegetables and ajwain, featuring slowly simmered tuna in coconut curry. Often garnished with lemon juice and green chillies .
steps: Prepare a masala paste with ground vegetables and ajwain.
Slowly simmer tuna in coconut milk with the masala paste.
Cook until the gravy thickens.
Garnish with lemon juice and green chillies before serving .
tip: A thick, flavourful tuna curry unique to Minicoy cuisine.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A thick, flavourful tuna curry unique to Minicoy cuisine.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best paired with Kirufoli (rice-flour crepe) .

title: Vegetable Kurma
description: Mixed vegetables cooked in a creamy coconut-based curry, influenced by Malabari cuisine and often served with chapati or rice .
steps: Sauté onion, garlic, ginger, and green chilli in oil.
Add vegetables and cook for a few minutes.
Add coconut milk and spices, simmer until vegetables are tender.
Garnish with curry leaves and serve with rice or chapati.
tip: A popular vegetarian option influenced by Kerala's Malabar cuisine .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A popular vegetarian option influenced by Kerala's Malabar cuisine .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Coconut milk gives the curry its creamy texture.

title: Octopus Fry
description: A Lakshadweep specialty - tender octopus pieces marinated with local spices, pepper, and curry leaves, then deep-fried or shallow-fried until crispy .
steps: Clean and cut octopus into bite-sized pieces.
Marinate with chilli powder, turmeric, pepper, ginger-garlic, and salt for 30 minutes.
Heat oil and shallow-fry until golden and crisp .
Garnish with curry leaves and serve hot.
tip: A rare treat in most of India - a unique Lakshadweep delicacy .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A rare treat in most of India - a unique Lakshadweep delicacy .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Can be pan-fried for a healthier version.

title: Garudiya (Full Meal Platter)
description: A complete Minicoy meal platter including clear tuna soup (Garudiya), Rihakuru fish sauce, Lonumirus (salty chilli-garlic paste), Mas-huni chutney, and rice .
steps: Prepare clear tuna soup (Garudiya) by simmering tuna with spices.
Serve with rice, Rihakuru sauce, Lonumirus paste, and Mas-huni chutney .
The meal is traditionally eaten as a complete platter.
tip: Rihakuru is a traditional fish sauce made by cooking fish in sea water for a week - it can stay for years without preservatives .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Rihakuru is a traditional fish sauce made by cooking fish in sea water for a week - it can stay for years without preservatives .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A traditional meal showcasing Minicoy's distinct culinary heritage.

title: Thalassery Seafood Biryani
description: A fragrant Kerala-style biryani adapted to Lakshadweep's coastal taste - made with seafood (fish or prawns) and chicken, cooked with coconut milk and local spices .
steps: Partially cook rice with whole spices.
Prepare a masala gravy with onion, ginger-garlic, and seafood/chicken.
Layer rice and meat gravy in a pot, add coconut milk and saffron.
Seal and cook on dum until done.
Serve with raita.
tip: A coastal twist on the beloved biryani - coconut, coriander, and saffron give it a special flavour .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A coastal twist on the beloved biryani - coconut, coriander, and saffron give it a special flavour .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Kavaratti Biryani is a local version with local spices .

title: Batla Appam
description: A sweet Androth Island delicacy resembling Southern Indian idlis but distinct in preparation - made with eggs, flour, sugar, and cardamom, steamed and served during festivities .
steps: Mix flour, eggs, sugar, cardamom, and salt into a smooth batter.
Pour into greased moulds (like idli moulds).
Steam for 12-15 minutes until cooked through .
Serve warm as a festive sweet.
tip: A festive favourite on Androth Island .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A festive favourite on Androth Island .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Similar to idlis but sweeter and made with eggs.

title: Kadalakka (Bengal Gram Cake)
description: A classic local dessert - a moist, wholesome cake made with chana dal (Bengal gram), eggs, cashews, and raisins. Also known as kadalakka pola or kadala pathil .
steps: Grind soaked chana dal into a fine paste.
Mix with eggs, sugar, cardamom, and nuts.
Pour into a greased pan and steam or pressure-cook until set .
Cool and cut into pieces.
tip: Often prepared in a pressure cooker for the perfect texture .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Often prepared in a pressure cooker for the perfect texture .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A nutritious sweet with generous amounts of cashews and raisins .

title: Lakshadweep Coconut Halwa (Aluva / Dweep Unda)
description: A traditional Lakshadweep halwa made from grated coconut, coconut water, and katti (local jaggery). Often packaged in dried banana leaves for long shelf life - historically carried by Haj pilgrims for 45-60 day sea journeys .
steps: Grate coconut kernels manually using traditional graters .
Melt katti (jaggery) in a pan - can be diluted with coconut water for enhanced taste .
Heat the mixture until it reaches one-string consistency.
Add coconut gratings and mix until uniformly coated .
Stir continuously under low flame until the mixture adheres to the ladle without sticking to the vessel .
Shape into balls while still hot.
Package in dried banana leaves, tied with banana leaf fibre .

fullIngredients.name: Fresh grated coconut (from 12-20 slightly immature coconuts)

tip: Traditional ladle is made from fresh coconut petiole - believed to make stirring easier .

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional ladle is made from fresh coconut petiole - believed to make stirring easier .

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Long shelf life - can stay fresh for months due to low moisture content (9-13%) .
